title: Sound Energy
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Every source of sound is touched while it sounds: a drum skin, a stretched rubber band, the throat while humming, a bottle blown across. Sound travel is tested with a string telephone and an ear on the desk while someone taps the far end.

skills.key_step: The child says sound is made when something vibrates, and finds the vibrating part in a source (a drum skin, a string, the air in a flute, the voice box).

floor.prerequisite: Knows a force can make things move.
floor.question: What does a force do to a still ball?

representations: a drum with rice grains on the skin
a hand on the throat while humming
steps: Find the part that moves back and forth.
Stop it moving: the sound stops.
contexts: a drum at a school festival

board.do: Draw a drum with rice grains on the skin.
Ask what the rice will do when the drum is hit.
Draw the grains jumping and write "the skin vibrates".

listen_for: the sound is in the drum
misconceptions.ask: What did the rice do when the drum was hit?

listen_for: the flute makes the sound, not the air
misconceptions.repair: In a flute or whistle, the air vibrates.

misconceptions.ask: How does a guitar or your voice make sound?
misconceptions.repair: Plucking, blowing and speaking make vibrations too.

misconceptions.ask: What happened when the skin was held still?
misconceptions.repair: Stop the vibration and the sound stops.

checks.question: What makes the sound when you pluck a guitar string?
What vibrates when you blow a whistle?

skills.key_step: The child says sound travels through solids, liquids and gases, travels better through solids, and cannot travel through empty space.

floor.prerequisite: Knows sound is made by vibrations.
floor.question: What vibrates in a drum?

representations: an ear on the desk while someone taps the far end
a picture of astronauts using radios
steps: Through air: we hear each other talk.
Through solids: tap the desk with an ear on it.
Through water: fish hear boats; swimmers hear clicks.
Space has no air, so no sound.
contexts: hearing a train through the rails

board.do: Draw two tins joined by a tight string.
Ask whether a whisper will be heard at the other end.
Write "sound travels along the string (a solid)".

misconceptions.ask: How did the whisper travel along the string?
misconceptions.repair: Sound travels through solids and liquids too.
Sound cannot travel through empty space.

misconceptions.ask: Why could you hear the tap better with your ear on the desk?
misconceptions.repair: Sound travels faster and better through solids.

misconceptions.ask: Do a shout and a whisper from far away reach you at different times?
misconceptions.repair: Loudness does not change the speed of sound.

checks.question: Why can astronauts not talk to each other in space without radios?
checks.answer: there is no air (no matter) for sound to travel through

skills.key_step: The child describes effects of loud sound (hearing damage that can be lasting, headaches, stress, trouble sleeping and learning) and ways to protect against it.
representations: a sound map of the school: loud and quiet places
steps: Name loud sources: machines, music, vehicles.
Hearing damage can last for life.
Protect: move away, turn down, cover the ears, limit time.
contexts: a posho mill next to a school

board.do: Draw a matatu with loud music.

board.say: What can loud music do to her ears over many days?

listen_for: it only hurts for a moment
misconceptions.repair: Loud sound can harm hearing for life and cause headaches.

misconceptions.ask: Does getting used to it stop the damage?
misconceptions.repair: Getting used to noise does not stop harm.

listen_for: music is pleasant so it is safe
misconceptions.ask: Is loud music still loud sound?
misconceptions.repair: Loud music can damage hearing too.

misconceptions.ask: How do learners feel after a day by a loud mill?
misconceptions.repair: Loud sound harms health and learning.

checks.question: Give one effect of very loud sound on people.
checks.answer: hearing damage, headaches, stress or poor sleep

checks.question: Give one way to protect your ears from loud sound.
checks.answer: move away, turn it down or cover your ears
